> **What you can defend when you leave.** Adapt one defensible claim to one audience and rehearse defending it against real questions.

## The milestone ahead {#checkpoint}

A claim becomes public the moment an audience can question it, and audiences do not read contracts. They read posters, hear talks, scan briefs, and ask hard questions. This milestone adapts your bounded claims to the format your venue asks for and rehearses the defense before it counts. The poster lessons carry the worked example; their audit transfers to whichever format you build. The rehearsal record matters as much as the artifact: the questions you cannot answer yet are the truest map of what remains.

This studio closes with **[Milestone 10: Your defense, ready](milestone10-adapt-and-defend.qmd)**, a short chapter of its own after the lessons. **What it asks you to produce.** One chosen format adaptation - poster, talk, brief, or another - plus a defense rehearsal record. This is not yet public release.

Milestone 11 lets strangers rerun what you have just defended, which is the one test rehearsal cannot give you. The milestone chapter keeps the working details: the practice steps, the versioned record, and how the artifact is assessed.

## Choosing your format

Your venue picks your format, and the lessons cover every route to it.
Read the row that fits, then work the lessons it names.

| If your venue asks for | build it with | then audit and rehearse with |
|---|---|---|
| a poster | Research Posters | Poster Criticism, then Difficult Questions |
| a talk or pitch | Research Pitches; slides follow the poster lesson's figure rules | Poster Criticism's audit, run on your slides, then Difficult Questions |
| a written brief or one-pager | Research Posters' one-figure discipline, in page form | Poster Criticism's audit, run on the page, then Difficult Questions |
| another format | the nearest row above, and name what transfers | the same audit, then Difficult Questions |

The poster is this book's fully worked example because it is the
hardest case: one surface, no narrator, every number exposed. The
audit taught in Poster Criticism (claim against boundary, hits ranked
by how far the error travels, three lenses, one revision, the lock
call) transfers to any format that carries your claim. Difficult
Questions is for everyone: whatever you build, you will answer for it.


## The lessons in this studio

Read them in order, working each lesson's **It is your turn** as you go. Each one builds a piece of Milestone 10; beside each lesson is the piece it hands you.

- [Lesson 31 — Research Posters](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part5-communicating/27-research-posters.html): if your venue is a poster (or your format borrows its one-figure discipline): the draft with labeled values, intervals drawn, and a headline verbed to your boundary.
- [Lesson 32 — Poster Criticism](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part5-communicating/28-poster-criticism.html): the audit of your chosen format's draft, hits ranked by how far the error travels, fixed once, and the lock call; the method is taught on the poster and transfers to any format.
- [Lesson 33 — Research Pitches](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part5-communicating/29-research-pitches.html): if you will speak: your 30-second and 3-minute pitches, built boundary-first and tested aloud on an outsider.
- [Lesson 34 — Difficult Questions and Uncertainty](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part5-communicating/30-difficult-questions-and-uncertainty.html): your five hardest fair questions with defend-or-concede answers, and your uncertainty-and-limitations statement in ULN form.

When the last lesson closes, the milestone chapter is next. Nothing you write in a lesson is busywork: every piece above is on the milestone's checklist.
